The absence of any GPS, timeline or chat record of the rider's presence or arrival during the whole 5 min 5 s wait (F2, F3, F11) means there is no record supporting her "came out a minute after" account, and NS-1 makes the system records, not the statement, the basis of the finding.

The rider's point about F12 is self-defeating: the system records (F2, F3, F5, F6) show the waiting and arrival conditions were satisfied, so the driver's written statement is consistent with, not contrary to, the records the judge relies on.

The rider's own NS-2 theory fails on the facts, because NS-1(i)-(iii) are all satisfied (F4, F6), so no flag_account under NS-2 arises; the profile history (F17) is account-review material only and cannot decide this case.
The refund remedy does not arise: the $6.61 fee (F7) was validly earned under NS-1 and, with no surge in play (F8), the correct disposition is no_action rather than a full refund.

The procedural point about the voucher is irrelevant once the fee is upheld: NS-7 governs how an upheld-against refund would be paid, not whether the driver earned the no-show fee, which NS-1 answers (F7).

what_would_change: Had the driver confirmed arrival more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled as a no-show, so the $6.61 is valid only if NS-1 is satisfied on all three elements; the system record shows he did tap 'I'm Here' while 41 m from the pickup point (F6), within the 200 m arrival radius, so element (ii) is met and the outcome turns on element (iii).

The driver pressed 'I'm Here' at 17:19:15 and cancelled at 17:22:55 (F6, F4) — exactly 3 min 40 s later, so the strict element (iii) bar of more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting measured from the tap is met; the rider does not dispute that arithmetic.

The driver's own chat confirms he treated the clock as running from his tap, not from his actual arrival: at 17:19 he said only 'I'm here at the pickup point' (F9) and at 17:22 he said '3 min up, cancelling the trip' (F10) — a 3-minute count that matches the tap at 17:19:15, showing the cancellation was triggered by his own timer rather than by the rider's failure to appear.

The platform's own arrival record is 17:17:50 (F5), and the driver was within 200 m from 17:17:50 with a cumulative 5 min 5 s inside that radius before cancelling (F2) and stationary only 54 m from the pickup point from 17:18:50 to the moment of cancellation (F3): whatever clock is used, he was present at the pickup for well over the threshold before he cancelled.

No system record contradicts that the rider was on her way out — the recorded timeline shows the gap between the driver's arrival confirmation and his cancellation is 5 min 5 s (F5), and nothing in the GPS, timeline or fare records shows the rider was unreachable or refused to board.

The driver's written statement that he 'waited over 3 minutes, nobody came' (F12) is a post-hoc statement and cannot outweigh the system records F2, F3, F5 and F6, which show he was at the pickup point and inside 200 m for the whole qualifying period.

The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days (F17), the same category as this one, so if the fee is found not to have been validly earned this is a repeat pattern rather than an isolated lapse.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is on record against the rider (F7) with no surge involved (F8), so a full refund of that item is the correct remedy and requires no further computation.
Any refund is to be issued as a Ryde voucher in the amount of the cancellation fee, and the dispute was filed by the rider on this ticket, within the 30-day window since the trip at 17:16–17:22.

weaknesses: The system records cut both ways: F2 shows the rider was inside/at the pickup point for 5 min 5 s and F3 shows the car stationary 54 m away for 4 min 5 s, which is the strongest proof for the driver that NS-1 (iii) was satisfied — he genuinely had a full waiting period and the rider only says she 'came out a minute after' the cancellation, which is a statement with no system corroboration.

The driver also has the chat messages F9 and F10 on his side: he announced his arrival and announced the 3-minute expiry before cancelling, which reads as ordinary no-show procedure; my reading that his 17:19:15 tap reset the clock is a reading of F6, and the judge may treat the 'continuous waiting' requirement as met either from the tap or from 17:17:50.

There is no record of the rider's own position or of any message from her during the wait (F11 lists only the driver's two messages), so the rider's account that she was one minute away is uncorroborated and F1/F2/F3 give the driver a clean presence record.
The driver's statement F12 contradicts the rider, and although NS-1 says system records win over statements, F12's substance is consistent with the system records rather than defeated by them.

claims.assertion: The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 while 41 m from the pickup point, i.e. within the 200 m arrival radius, satisfying NS-1(i) and (ii).
After the "I'm Here" tap the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup point for 3 min 40 s, exceeding the >3 minutes continuous-wait requirement before cancelling at 17:22:55, so NS-1(iii) is met.

The GPS and timeline records corroborate the driver's account: he was first inside 200 m at 17:17:50, stationary 4 min 5 s at 54 m from the pickup until cancellation, giving 5 min 5 s cumulative time inside 200 m before he cancelled.

The driver gave notice of arrival in writing at 17:19 ("I'm here at the pickup point, black Hyundai Ioniq") and warned at 17:22 that 3 minutes were up before cancelling, so the cancellation followed notice rather than being an unexplained abandonment.
Because NS-1(i)-(iii) are all satisfied, the $6.61 passenger no-show cancellation fee stands and the rider's complaint should not change the fare.
The chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped), so there is no evidence gap requiring the case to be referred to a human under the incompleteness rule.

The driver's 90-day history shows 2 upheld no-show disputes, but that profile fact may support at most an additional account-review action and cannot decide this case, which is already resolved on the GPS/timeline records.

weaknesses: NS-1(iii) measures continuous waiting after the 'I'm Here' tap; the tap at 17:19:15 leaves 3 min 40 s to cancellation, which clears the >3 min bar by only 40 seconds — the rider will argue the driver's own margin is thin (F6, F4).

The driver's closest approach was 35 m and he was stationary at 54 m from the pickup point (F1, F3); the rider may argue he never came fully to the pickup point, though NS-1(ii) only requires being within the 200 m radius (F6), and the platform itself recorded arrival at 17:17:50 (F5).

The rider's complaint that she 'came out a minute after' the cancellation is not contradicted by any GPS or chat record of her arriving, but equally no record shows she was present within 200 m during the 5 min 5 s wait (F2, F3) — the finding rests on the absence of her arrival in the records.
The driver's record of 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) gives the rider a fairness argument for stricter scrutiny and may invite dispute history to be weighed against him.

points.response: Conceded as to the elements it addresses: the tap at 17:19:15 at 41 m (F6) does satisfy NS-1(i) and (ii), which is why the rider's case rests on element (iii), not on the arrival moment.

Element (iii) requires continuous waiting after the tap until cancellation, and the driver's own margin is the point: 17:19:15 to 17:22:55 is 3 min 40 s (F6, F4), only 40 seconds past the >3:00 bar — the driver cancelled on his own timer at the earliest permissible second rather than giving the rider the benefit of any margin, which is exactly the conduct NS-1(iii) is meant to police.

F2 and F3 show only that the car was parked near the pickup point, not that the rider was absent; the driver's 17:22 message '3 min up, cancelling the trip' (F10) shows he counted from his 17:19:15 tap (F6), not from his 17:17:50 platform arrival (F5), so the record proves presence in the radius, not expiry of the NS-1 waiting period before the rider could arrive.

The messages (F9, F10) are the driver's own notices and cannot convert his conduct into compliance; NS-1 turns on the system records and the timing of the cancellation, and F10's '3 min up' confirms he cancelled at the 3-minute mark he set for himself rather than after any evidence the rider had failed to appear.

The $6.61 fee stands only if NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) are all met (NS-0), and the rider's position is that the one-minute turn-around time plus the 17:22:55 cancellation at the very edge of the 3-minute window (F4, F10) makes the fee unearned, so the fee should be refunded rather than left in place.

Completeness of the chat (F11) is not in dispute, but a complete chat still shows no message from the rider during the wait period; the record resolves nothing about the rider's arrival and the driver's thin 3-minute margin remains on F6 and F4.

The rider agrees profile facts (F17) cannot decide the no-show issue; they are relevant only as a supporting action if the fee is found unearned, given the two prior upheld no-show disputes in the same 90-day window.

Agreed on the framework: element (ii) is met because the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:19:15 while 41 m from the pickup point (F6), and the case therefore turns on element (iii), which the system records establish in the driver's favour.

This claim concedes the arithmetic of the driver's client: 17:22:55 minus the 17:19:15 tap is 3 min 40 s, which exceeds the >3 min continuous-wait bar in NS-1(iii), so the rider's own advocate agrees the fee condition is made out (F4, F6).

Nothing in NS-1 requires the driver to ignore his own tap clock: the clause measures continuous waiting from the "I'm Here" tap onward, and the driver's 17:22 message (F10) simply reports that the measure was complete before he cancelled (F6).

This claim is the rider's own strongest concession and I adopt it: the driver was inside 200 m from 17:17:50 for a cumulative 5 min 5 s (F2) and stationary 54 m away for 4 min 5 s up to the cancellation (F3), so the qualifying wait holds on any clock the judge prefers (F5).

The absence of any GPS, timeline or chat record of the rider's presence or arrival during the whole 5 min 5 s wait (F2, F3, F11) means there is no record supporting her "came out a minute after" account, and NS-1 makes the system records, not the statement, the basis of the finding.

The rider's point about F12 is self-defeating: the system records (F2, F3, F5, F6) show the waiting and arrival conditions were satisfied, so the driver's written statement is consistent with, not contrary to, the records the judge relies on.

The rider's own NS-2 theory fails on the facts, because NS-1(i)-(iii) are all satisfied (F4, F6), so no flag_account under NS-2 arises; the profile history (F17) is account-review material only and cannot decide this case.
The refund remedy does not arise: the $6.61 fee (F7) was validly earned under NS-1 and, with no surge in play (F8), the correct disposition is no_action rather than a full refund.

The procedural point about the voucher is irrelevant once the fee is upheld: NS-7 governs how an upheld-against refund would be paid, not whether the driver earned the no-show fee, which NS-1 answers (F7).

notices.text:
We reviewed your dispute about the no-show cancellation fee and did not change the outcome: the fee stands and no refund is issued.

What decided it: the driver was recorded at the pickup point when he marked he had arrived, and stayed within the pickup area for longer than the required wait before cancelling. Our system also shows no record of you arriving or boarding during that wait.

The driver's account is noted for routine monitoring only — it did not affect this decision.

Nothing else changes for you: your account is not flagged and no amount is owed or paid out.

We reviewed the rider's dispute of your no-show cancellation fee. Outcome: the fee stands and no refund is issued to the rider.

What decided it: your arrival tap placed you at the pickup point, and the location record shows you stayed inside the pickup area longer than the required wait before you cancelled.

No account action follows for you: your account is not flagged and your standing is unchanged. A note about your dispute history is kept for routine monitoring only and did not affect this ruling.

No payment is due from you, and nothing else is required.
